description: The line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC, in percentage) of five different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, and ROME—across varying co-occurrence numbers, with the x-axis representing the co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to 1000, and the y-axis showing accuracy from 60% to 85%. The Base method, represented by black circles connected by a solid line, starts at approximately 63.5% and increases steadily to about 72.5%. The MEND method, shown with brown diamonds and a solid line, begins at around 71.5% and rises to approximately 80.5%. The FT method, depicted with blue triangles and a solid line, starts at about 65.5% and increases to roughly 73.5%. The MEMIT method, represented by purple squares and a solid line, begins at approximately 69.5% and climbs to about 77.5%. The ROME method, shown with green squares and a solid line, starts at around 74.5% and increases to approximately 83.5%. All methods show a general upward trend in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases, with ROME consistently achieving the highest accuracy across all co-occurrence numbers.
